sources.citation: Antoine Lutz, Lawrence L. Greischar, Nancy B. Rawlings, Matthieu Ricard et al. (2004). Long-term meditators self-induce high-amplitude gamma synchrony during mental practice. Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences.
sources.notes: Foundational primary study (2004) in Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences establishing the core experimental paradigm and quantitative parameters.

sources.citation: Antoine Lutz, Heleen A. Slagter, Nancy B. Rawlings, Andrew D. Francis, Lawrence L. Greischar, Richard J. Davidson (2009). Mental Training Enhances Attentional Stability: Neural and Behavioral Evidence. Journal of Neuroscience.
sources.notes: Three-month intensive meditation training study demonstrating increased frontal-theta phase consistency and reduced reaction-time variability.

sources.citation: Fabio Ferrarelli, Richard Smith, Daniela Dentico, Brady A. Riedner, Corinna Zennig, Ruth M. Benca, Antoine Lutz, Richard J. Davidson, Giulio Tononi (2013). Experienced Mindfulness Meditators Exhibit Higher Parietal-Occipital EEG Gamma Activity during NREM Sleep. PLoS ONE.
sources.notes: Records elevated parietal-occipital gamma power during muscle-relaxed non-REM sleep in long-term meditators, ruling out waking cranial EMG artifact.

sources.citation: S Haupt, N Axmacher, CE Elger, J Fell (2007). Working memory load affects long-term memory formation. Neuro-Visionen 4.
sources.notes: Subsequent empirical and theoretical investigation (2007) in Neuro-Visionen 4 extending the foundational findings.

sources.citation: Nikolai Axmacher, Sarah Lenz, Sven Haupt, Christian E. Elger et al. (2010). Electrophysiological signature of working and long‐term memory interaction in the human hippocampus. European Journal of Neuroscience.
sources.notes: Subsequent empirical and theoretical investigation (2010) in European Journal of Neuroscience extending the foundational findings.

sources.citation: Antoine Lutz, Heleen A. Slagter, John D. Dunne, Richard J. Davidson (2008). Attention regulation and monitoring in meditation. Trends in Cognitive Sciences.
sources.notes: Neurocognitive synthesis distinguishing focused-attention from open-monitoring meditation networks by Lutz and Davidson.
